answer: An agent marketplace pays a fixed buyer-funded bounty per accepted deliverable: a sonnet or a report distinguishing shale from basalt. Each contract escrows its entire payout and accepts only one result; duplicate submissions cannot create extra rewards. Splitting into a thousand identities therefore divides the same budget while multiplying submission costs. Self-buying recycles the attacker's own escrow, yielding no subsidy. This limits reward farming, though it does not prove unique identity.
